info.title: Ownkube CLI API
info.description: API for the Ownkube CLI tool. Authenticate via browser-based flow, then use x-api-key header for subsequent requests.

organizations.description: Organizations this user belongs to. Pass an `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when membership is plural.

quickCreateUrl.description: Open in a browser and click Create stack (handoff mode)

AwsConnectTemplate.description: Deploy this stack yourself with AWS creds already in your environment (autonomous mode). Parameter keys match the template exactly.

awsAccountId.description: 12-digit AWS account ID once the stack reports in

status.description: pending (waiting on the stack) / configuring (provisioning access) / verified / failed

code.description: Raw CloudFormation status code this maps from

kind.description: How to recover: `retry` (transient/propagation, re-verify or re-launch the same stack), `quota` (fix an AWS limit then re-verify), `conflict` (account claimed elsewhere, use a different account).

description.description: What happened and what to do next

AwsConnectionFailure.description: Structured failure + remediation when status is `failed`

available.description: Whether the Ownkube Compute deploy path is currently open.

regions.description: Regions you can deploy to on Ownkube Compute. Pass a region `id` here as the `region` field when creating a deployment with no `clusterId`.

enabled.description: Whether Ownkube Compute (and its wallet) is available here.

loadedInByReason.description: Total credit loaded into the wallet, in USD, keyed by inflow reason (e.g. plan load, top-up, signup credit).

CreditBalance.description: Live wallet balance, or null if the org has none yet.

enabled.description: Whether Ownkube Compute is available here.

monthlyBudgetUsd.description: Optional monthly spend cap, in USD. Null means no budget cap is set.

budgetAction.description: What happens at the budget cap: `notify` only alerts; `pause` suspends compute (data retained) like wallet exhaustion.

alertThresholdsPct.description: Percent-of-budget thresholds that fire a spend alert.

SpendControls.description: The org's spend controls, or null when compute is off.

enabled.description: Whether Ownkube Compute (and its wallet) is available here.

claimed.description: Whether the one-time signup credit has already been claimed.

amountUsd.description: The signup-credit grant amount, in USD.

topUpMinUsd.description: Minimum custom wallet top-up amount, in USD.

alreadyClaimed.description: True if the credit was already claimed (nothing new granted).

url.description: Browser checkout URL. Open it to complete payment; the account updates once the payment settles.

tier.description: The plan to subscribe to: `personal` ($5/mo) or `team` ($20/mo). Each loads that much wallet credit every cycle.

amountUsd.description: Amount to add to the wallet, in USD. Must be at least the top-up minimum (see `topUpMinUsd` on GET /v1/credit).

hourlyCostUsd.description: Current burn rate, in USD per hour, across everything.

starterClusters.description: Count of active flat-priced Starter clusters.

costUsd.description: Gross month-to-date cost drawn from the wallet, in USD.

projectedCostUsd.description: Straight-line projected wallet draw for the month, in USD.

slug.description: Lowercase, starts with a letter; letters, numbers, hyphens only.

secret.description: Mark as secret so the value is never returned on reads. Echo a saved secret back with an empty `value` to keep the previous value.

env.description: The full shared env-var set for the environment (replaces the existing set). Every cluster-bound app in the environment is redeployed to apply it.

fields.description: Structured fields, keyed by their published label.

restartedAt.description: The restart timestamp stamped on the pod template.

message.description: Optional line shown on the maintenance page. Ignored when disabling.

displayName.description: Cosmetic display label. Empty/whitespace clears it (falls back to the immutable name).

contextPath.description: Root directory for the build, relative to the repo root. Empty string clears it.

current.description: True when the label is the one this deployment already holds.

hostname.description: The host to link — a subdomain or the apex of a parent.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: API key issued by the browser-based CLI authorization flow.

get.description: Returns the profile of the user associated with the provided API key.

get.summary: List organizations the API key's user belongs to
get.description: Use the returned `id` as the `x-ownkube-organization` header on subsequent requests when your account belongs to more than one org.

post.description: Mints a cross-account access request and returns the CloudFormation artifacts. Reuses this org's in-flight (unproven) row, so repeated calls do not pile up records. Poll GET /v1/aws/accounts/{accountId} until status is `verified` or `failed`.

delete.description: Blocked while any cluster still references the account (the cross-account role is required to tear infra down). Destroy those clusters first.

post.description: Normally the stack's phone-home finalizes the connection automatically. Call this to force a verify, optionally passing `awsAccountId` to assume the role directly before the callback arrives.

schema.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.

parameters.description: 12-digit AWS account ID. Supply it to verify immediately (autonomous mode) instead of waiting for the stack's phone-home.
parameters.name: awsAccountId

post.summary: Re-arm an account whose access stack was removed
post.description: Re-arms the existing row in place (same external ID and account ID) and returns a fresh CloudFormation link. Re-running the stack recreates the role and re-verifies the same account, so no duplicate is created.

post.summary: Re-run account setup on a verified account
post.description: Re-applies the shared roles and policies for an already-verified account. Safe to call to pick up an available upgrade (`needsUpgrade: true`).

get.summary: List clusters in the current organization

post.description: Provisions a cluster (`clusterType` selects the shape: `eks` = Production, the self-hosted shape = Starter) into a verified AWS account (`cloudAccountId`). Returns immediately with a `clusterId` and `status: creating`; poll `/v1/clusters/{clusterId}/status` until it reports `active` or `failed`.

delete.description: Tears the cluster down. Blocked when the cluster still has active deployments unless `force=true` is passed.

schema.description: Destroy even when the cluster still has active deployments. Defaults to false.

parameters.description: Destroy even when the cluster still has active deployments. Defaults to false.
parameters.name: force

get.summary: Get a cluster's live provisioning status
get.description: Lightweight poll target during create/destroy: status, message, and provisioning progress without the full row.

post.description: Valid only while the cluster is still `creating`.

get.description: Lists the regions available for deploying on Ownkube Compute (the shared, no-cluster path). Use a returned region `id` as the `region` field on `POST /v1/deployments` while omitting `clusterId`. `available: false` (empty `regions`) means the Compute path is off.
Returns the live wallet balance (granted, consumed, remaining) plus how much credit was loaded by inflow reason. Check this before deploying on Ownkube Compute — a deploy needs a positive balance.
Returns the org's optional monthly budget cap, what happens at the cap, and the spend-alert thresholds.

put.description: Creates or updates the monthly budget cap and spend alerts. Set `budgetAction: pause` to actually cap the bill (suspends compute, data retained, at the cap); `notify` only alerts. Only the fields you pass are changed.

get.summary: Get account credit and claim status
get.description: Returns whether the one-time signup credit is still claimable, the signup grant amount, the live wallet balance, and the wallet top-up minimum.

post.description: Grants the one-time signup credit to fund a first Ownkube Compute deploy. Idempotent — re-claiming returns the current balance and grants nothing new. Availability is gated per account; a `403` means the signup credit isn't offered to this account yet.
Creates a customer-portal session and returns a browser `url` to manage payment method, invoices, and subscription. A `412` means the org has no billing account yet (start a plan first).
Creates a checkout for a monthly plan (Personal or Team). Returns a browser `url` to complete payment; the subscription loads wallet credit each cycle once active.

Creates a checkout to add a custom amount of credit to the organization's prepaid wallet. Returns a browser `url` to complete payment; the balance updates once the payment settles. A `400` means the amount is below the top-up minimum.

get.description: Current metered vCPU + memory in use and the resulting hourly cost across everything the org runs.
Usage totals (vCPU-hours, memory-GiB-hours, egress) and the gross cost drawn from the wallet so far this calendar month.
Naive straight-line projection of the month's wallet draw (month-to-date cost scaled to the full month). Volatile early in the month.
Per-day usage and cost for the current calendar month, zero-filled for a continuous series.

get.summary: List environments in the current organization
get.description: Default `Development` and `Production` environments are auto-seeded for orgs that have none yet, so this endpoint always returns at least two rows.

patch.summary: Update an environment's name, color, or description

delete.description: Soft-deletes the environment. Blocked with `412` if any deployments still reference it.

put.summary: Replace an environment's shared env vars
put.description: Replaces the environment's shared env-var set and redeploys every cluster-bound app that inherits them so the change takes effect immediately.

get.description: Pass `environmentId` to scope to one environment, or `clusterId` to scope to one cluster. Omit both to list the organization's Ownkube Compute deployments (the shared, no-cluster deploy path). Passing both is an error.

post.description: Creates a deployment. The body is a discriminated union on `resourceType` (`web`, `worker`, `job`, `database`, `function`); each type carries its own `config` block. Omit `clusterId` on a cluster-bound type to deploy onto the org's shared cluster.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the deployment and tears down its cluster resources. Functions hand off to an async teardown and report `deleting` until it finalizes.

patch.description: Updates a cluster-bound deployment (web/worker/job/database) and records a revision. Send the config block matching the deployment's type: `appConfig` for web/worker, `jobConfig` for job, `databaseConfig` for database. Use the function update endpoint for functions.

get.description: Reads log lines from the in-cluster logs backend over the requested window. `filter` accepts a LogsQL regex matched against the message body.
Returns the host, port, credentials, and connection URI for a database deployment. Only valid for `resourceType: database`.
Returns the host, port, password, and connection URI for a cache deployment. Only valid for `resourceType: cache`.

patch.description: Updates a `function`-type deployment's config (handler, runtime, env, triggers) and records a revision.

post.summary: Copy a deployment to another environment
post.description: Clones this deployment's current config into `targetEnvironmentId` on `targetClusterId`, creating a new deployment. Not valid for functions.
Rotates the owner-role password of a `database`-type deployment and returns the new password. The response intentionally contains the live credential.

get.summary: List a scheduled job's recent runs
get.description: Reads the CronJob and its spawned runs live from the cluster. Non-job deployments return an empty, non-existent history rather than erroring.

post.description: Spawns a one-off run of a `job`-type deployment off-schedule and returns the created Job name.

delete.description: Deletes the named run's Job (terminating its Pods). The named Job must belong to this deployment's CronJob.

post.summary: Recover a database to an earlier point in time
post.description: Destructive, in-place point-in-time recovery of a `database`-type deployment: WIPES the current volume and rebuilds the database from its own automated backups at `targetTime` (omit for the latest point). Requires backups to be enabled. This cannot be undone.

schema.description: RFC3339 recovery target. Omit to replay to the latest available point.

parameters.description: RFC3339 recovery target. Omit to replay to the latest available point.
parameters.name: targetTime

post.description: Rollout-restarts a running web or worker deployment (replaces every pod with the same image). Not a rebuild and not a new revision. Only valid for web/worker deployments that are already live.

put.description: Enables or disables auto-deploy on a source-backed deployment. Reuses the branch captured at create time. Rejected for deployments without a source repository.

put.summary: Turn maintenance mode on or off
put.description: Diverts a public web deployment's URL to a branded maintenance page (the workload keeps running). Only valid once public access is on and the first build has completed.
Sets (or clears) the cosmetic display label. Never touches the immutable name / cluster identity, cuts no revision, and does not re-sync.
Replaces the custom build-time arguments for a deployment that builds on your cluster. Applies on the next build. An empty map clears them.
Sets the root directory (build context) for a deployment that builds on your cluster — how a monorepo app in a subdirectory gets built. Applies on the next build. Empty string clears it.
Sets the build pod's size (small / standard / large) for a deployment that builds on your cluster. Applies on the next build. On Ownkube Compute, `large` requires the Team plan.

get.summary: Check if an address label is available
get.description: Checks whether an address label is legal and free right now for this deployment. `current: true` means it's the label the deployment already holds.
Returns a handful of address labels that are free right now, seeded from the deployment name (or the `desired` seed) and namespaced with the environment and organization when they read well.

schema.description: Seed the suggestions from what the user has typed so far.

parameters.description: Seed the suggestions from what the user has typed so far.
parameters.name: desired

put.description: Moves a public web app to a chosen address label and re-syncs its route. The old address stops resolving. Not valid for databases (their certificate is issued for the hostname).

get.summary: List revisions for a deployment (newest first)

post.summary: Roll a deployment back to a prior revision
post.description: Restores the config snapshot from `revisionId` onto the deployment and records a new revision. Returns the new revision.

post.summary: Promote a deployment's config to another deployment
post.description: Copies this deployment's current config into `targetDeploymentId`, records a revision there, and links it back to this deployment's latest revision. Returns the new revision on the target.

Rebuilds an in-cluster deployment from the current head of its tracked branch — the manual counterpart to the push trigger. Queues a build and supersedes any in-flight one. Only valid for deployments that build from source.

schema.description: Optional note recorded on the queued revision.

parameters.description: Optional note recorded on the queued revision.
parameters.name: note

get.summary: Get overview telemetry (CPU, memory, requests, latency)
get.description: Reads the overview telemetry tiles — CPU, memory, request rate, and p95 latency — over the requested window. Returns `null` when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

Reads the expanded observability panel — per-status-class request rate, latency percentiles, and CPU/memory time-series — over the requested window. `hasRequestData` is false for workloads whose gateway doesn't report per-deployment request telemetry. Returns `null` when the cluster isn't reachable yet.
Reads database-shaped telemetry — connections, disk usage, database size, CPU, memory, and transaction rate. Returns `null` for non-database deployments or when the cluster isn't reachable yet.
Reads cache-shaped telemetry — connected clients, memory, ops/sec, hit rate, CPU, and disk. Returns `null` for non-cache deployments or when the cluster isn't reachable yet.

Reads invocation-shaped telemetry — invocations, errors, duration, throttles, and concurrency — for a function deployment. Returns `null` for non-function deployments or when the function isn't provisioned yet.

Reads the build output for one revision — the live build pod while a build is in flight, else the durable log store once the build settles. Best-effort: returns an empty log rather than erroring when no build output is available.

get.summary: List alert rules for a deployment (newest first)

post.description: Creates a metric alert rule on an Ownkube Compute deployment. `metric` is `cpu`/`memory` (percent of the app's limit, threshold ≤ 100) or `restarts` (a raw count). Only valid for Ownkube Compute deployments.

patch.description: Edits an alert rule's fields or toggles `enabled`. All body fields are optional; percent metrics still cap the threshold at 100.

get.description: Lists recent alert firings for the organization, optionally scoped to one deployment. A firing is recorded when a rule starts breaching and updated to `resolved` when it recovers.

get.summary: List a deployment's linked custom domains
get.description: Lists the hosts linked to this web app plus the parent domains registered on its cluster that are available to link. Each linked host carries the DNS record the customer sets to route it.

post.summary: Link a custom domain to a deployment
post.description: Links a host (a subdomain like `app.customer.com`, or the apex `customer.com`) to a public web app. The host's parent domain must already be registered on the app's cluster. Returns the linked host with the DNS record to create.
Re-runs the reconcile for a linked host and reports the parent certificate status. The host goes live once its routing record resolves and the certificate is active.

delete.description: Detaches a host from its deployment. The parent domain stays registered on the cluster for other apps.
